# Remote AC Controller v1.2.1

## Who should use this release

- Anyone who builds the firmware or deploys the cloud stack — this is a
  presentation/documentation and PCB-correction release.
- **Anyone who plans to manufacture the PCB must use this release** (or newer):
  the v1.2.0 auto-generated source archives contain pre-correction PCB files.

## Important PCB notice

- The PCB design revision is now **Rev 1.0.1** (software release vs PCB
  revision are separated).
- Rev 1.0 manufacturing files are superseded and must not be used.
- The manufacturing package
  `remote-ac-controller-pcb-rev1.0.1.zip` is built deterministically from
  Git-controlled bytes; per-file hashes are in `manufacturing-manifest.md`.
- A verified BOM and pick-and-place file are **not** included.

## Highlights

- Bilingual READMEs re-architected for developers.
- Community files (CONTRIBUTING / SECURITY / SUPPORT) are actionable guides.
- Maintainer documentation (release process, versioning, PCB release) added
  in both languages.
- Startup banner no longer shows a double "v" (`firmware v1.2.1`).
- Manufacturing bytes are protected by `.gitattributes` and deterministic
  packaging.

## Compatibility

- Firmware and cloud behavior remain compatible with v1.2.0.
- **No cloud API or database schema changes.**
- PCB manufacturing users must use Rev 1.0.1.

## Assets

- Source archives (auto-generated zip / tar.gz)
- `remote-ac-controller-pcb-rev1.0.1.zip` — PCB manufacturing package
- `remote-ac-controller-ir-simple-learner-src-v1.2.1.zip` — IR learning tool
- `IR_Simple_Learner_v4.exe` — IR learning tool (Windows)
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` — asset hashes

## Upgrade notes

- Firmware/cloud users can upgrade freely; no schema or API migration is
  needed.
- Re-download all assets from this release and verify `SHA256SUMS.txt` before
  use.

## Known issues

- A verified BOM or pick-and-place file is not provided.
- Real AC IR frames are not shipped in the public repository; capture your own
  with the IR learning tool.
- v1.2.0 auto-generated source archives still contain the old PCB files — do
  not manufacture from them.
